Our GRG World Supercentenarian Rankings List is available below. By definition, a supercentenarian is anyone who has been validated to have lived to be 110 or over.

- Since the death of 116-year-old Inah Canabarro Lucas of Brazil on 30 April 2025, Ethel Caterham(born 21 August 1909) of the United Kingdom is the oldest living person whose age is validated.
- Since the death of 112-year-old John Tinniswood of the United Kingdom on 25 November 2024, João Marinho Neto(born 5 October 1912) of Brazil is the oldest living man whose age is validated.

results.title: Ethel Caterham
results.text:
Ethel Caterham

Ethel May Caterham (née Collins; born 21 August 1909) is an English supercentenarian who, at the age of 116 years, 317 days, has been the world's oldest verified living person since the death of Inah Canabarro Lucas on 30 April 2025. She is the oldest British person in recorded history, the 16th oldest person in history, the last surviving validated individual born in the 1900s decade, and the last surviving subject of King Edward VII.

| Ethel Caterham | - |
| --- | --- |
| Born | Ethel May Collins, (1909-08-21)21 August 1909, (age 116 years, 317 days), Shipton Bellinger, Hampshire, England |
| Known for | Oldest verified living person (since 30 April 2025), Oldest British person ever |
| Spouse | Norman Caterham, ​, ​(m. 1933; died 1976)​ |
| Children | 2 |

## Biography

### Early life and family

Ethel May Collins was born on 21 August 1909 in Shipton Bellinger, Hampshire, England, as the second youngest of eight siblings. She spent her early years in the nearby town of Tidworth. Her sister, Gladys Babilas, reached the age of 104. In 1927, at 18 years old, Caterham travelled to British India, where she worked as an au pair for a military household until the age of 21.

In 1931, following her return to England, she met Norman Caterham at a dinner party. The couple were married at Salisbury Cathedral in 1933, where Norman had previously sung as a choirboy. He went on to serve as a lieutenant colonel in the Royal Army Pay Corps. They lived in Harnham, Salisbury before postings in Hong Kong and Gibraltar. During their time in Hong Kong, she established a nursery school focused on English language, crafts and recreational activities. While stationed in Gibraltar, the couple had two daughters, Gem and Anne, whom they later raised in England. Norman died in 1976, and Gem died in the early 2000s.

### Later years

Caterham drove until she was 97 and enjoyed playing contract bridge in her centenarian years. Both of her daughters predeceased her, but she has three grandchildren and five great-grandchildren. She had lived in an annex within the home of her younger daughter, Anne, until Anne's death in February 2020 at the age of 82. Following this, Caterham relocated to a care facility in Ash Vale, Surrey, and later moved to another home in Lightwater.

In 2020, at the age of 110, Caterham contracted and recovered from COVID-19. Shortly before her 111th birthday, she was interviewed by BBC Radio Surrey, where she attributed her longevity to "taking everything in my stride, the highs and the lows." On her 111th birthday in August 2020, she was visited by the mayor of Surrey Heath, having been the oldest living resident of Surrey since January 2019.

On 22 January 2022, following the death of Mary "Mollie" Walker, Caterham became the oldest living person in the United Kingdom. On 7 October 2022, after the death of Rose Eaton, she became the last known surviving subject of Edward VII. Upon turning 115 in August 2024, Caterham became the third British person verified to reach this age, and the first to do so since Annie Jennings in 1999. On 7 April 2025, Caterham surpassed Charlotte Hughes' age, to become the oldest person ever from the United Kingdom. On 30 April 2025, following the death of Inah Canabarro Lucas of Brazil, Caterham became both the world's oldest living person and the last known individual born in the 1900s decade.

On 21 August 2025, Caterham celebrated her 116th birthday, becoming the first person in British history to reach this age. She received a congratulatory message from João Marinho Neto of Brazil (born 5 October 1912), the world's oldest living man– reportedly the first documented exchange between the world's oldest verified woman and oldest verified man.

In September 2025, Caterham, the last living subject of King Edward VII, met his great-great grandson King Charles III, with whom she exchanged pleasantries and recalled his investiture in 1969.

This article is about the oldest currently living people. For specific supercentenarian claims validated by modern standards, see [List of the verified oldest people](./List_of_the_verified_oldest_people). For the oldest verified people of all time, see [Oldest people](./Oldest_people). For contemporary unvalidated supercentenarian claims, see [Longevity claims](./Longevity_claims).
This is a list of the oldest living people who have been verified to be alive as of the dates of the cited supporting sources. It was estimated in 2015 that between 150 and 600 living people had reached the age of 110. The true number is uncertain, as not all [supercentenarians](./Supercentenarian) are known to researchers at a given time, and some claims cannot be validated or are fraudulent. Nearly all the top 50 oldest living people are women, as women live longer than men on average. A [list of the oldest living men](./Oldest_living_people#Oldest_living_men) is provided below the main list.
* [Ethel Caterham](./Ethel_Caterham) (born 21 August 1909) of the United Kingdom is the world's oldest living person whose age has been validated.
* [João Marinho Neto](./João_Marinho_Neto) (born 5 October 1912) of Brazil is the world's oldest living man whose age has been validated.

List of oldest people

The following are tables of the oldest people in the world in ordinal ranks. To avoid including false or unconfirmed claims of old age, names here are restricted to those people whose ages have been validated by an international body dealing in longevity research, such as the Gerontology Research Group, LongeviQuest, or Guinness World Records, and others who have otherwise been reliably sourced.

The longest documented and verified human lifespan is that of Jeanne Calment of France(1875–1997), a woman who lived to the age of 122 years and 164 days. As women live longer than men on average, women predominate in combined records. The longest lifespan for a man is that of Jiroemon Kimura of Japan(1897–2013), who lived to the age of 116 years and 54 days.

The oldest living person in the world whose age has been validated is Ethel Caterham of the United Kingdom, who has lived 116 years, 265 days. She was born on 21 August 1909. The oldest living verified man is João Marinho Neto of Brazil, who has lived 113 years, 220 days. He was born on 5 October 1912.

## Ten oldest verified people

Systematic verification of longevity has only been practiced since the 1950s and only in certain parts of the world. All ten oldest verified people ever are female.

The longest documented and verified human lifespan is that of Jeanne Calment of France, a woman who lived to age 122 years and 164 days. She received news media attention in 1985, after turning 110. Calment's claim was investigated and authenticated by Jean-Marie Robine and Dr. Michel Allard for the Gerontology Research Group(GRG). Her longevity claim was put into question in 2018, but the original assessing team stood by their judgement.

List of the verified oldest people

These are lists of the 100 known verified oldest people sorted in descending order by age in years and days. The oldest person ever whose age has been independently verified is Jeanne Calment(1875–1997) of France, who lived to the age of 122 years and 164 days. The oldest verified man ever is Jiroemon Kimura(1897–2013) of Japan, who lived to the age of 116 years and 54 days.

The oldest known living person is Ethel Caterham of the United Kingdom, aged 116 years, 336 days. The oldest known living man is João Marinho Neto of Brazil, aged 113 years, 291 days. The 100 oldest women have, on average, lived several years longer than the 100 oldest men.

results.title: Who is the oldest person in the world in 2024?
results.text:
Who is the oldest person in the world in 2024? | BBC Science Focus Magazine

The verifiably oldest ever person in the world is Jeanne Louise Calment, who lived to the age of 122 years and 164 days old.

It’s incredible to imagine what Calment and today's supercentenarians (people who are 110 years old or older) have witnessed in their lifetimes. Just think what it must have been like to be a teenager in the 1920s, to have lived through both World Wars, to have watched the first Moon landings in your fifties or sixties, and then still be alive at the end of the 21st century to observe the latest scientific and technological advances unfold so quickly and dramatically.

Today, the oldest person alive (as of August 2025), is the UK's Ethel Caterham. She is a sprightly 116 years, an age well beyond the average life expectancy of a human.

In the UK, the average life expectancy of a man is 78.8 years, and a woman 82.8 years, according to the Office for National Statistics. Expectancy is a bit lower in the US, with males expected to live 75.8 years, and women 81.1.

With different cultural, hygienic, and scientific reasons, average life expectancy around the world changes depending on which country you live in and even where in that country you live.

The UN estimates that the worldwide life expectancy is now 73.3 years– that's about nine years longer than people lived in 1995.

## Who is the oldest person alive today?

The oldest living person as of August 2025 is Ethel Caterham. She is 116 years old.

She was born on 21 August 1909 in Hampshire, UK, during the reign of Edward VII. She currently lives in a nursing home in Lightwater, Surrey.

According to the Guinness World Records, she was the second of eight children. Remarkably, her older sister Gladys Babilas also made it past the 100 mark, living to 104 years and 78 days.

Her husband, whom she first met back in 1931, died in 1976, leaving behind his classic Triumph Dolomite car, which she still drove until the age of 97. Tragically, she also outlived both of her children.

## Previous title holders

### Jeanne Louise Calment - Oldest person ever

120-year-old Jeanne Louise Calment sitting in armchair at home © Ian Cook/Getty Images

Jeanne Louise Calment is the oldest verified person to have ever lived. The Frenchwoman lived to the ripe old age of 122 years and 164 days old. She was born on 21 February 1875 and passed away aged 122 on 4 August 1997.

According to Guinness World Records, Calment “ate almost 1kg of chocolate” every week, and smoked “from the age of 21 and only quit when she was 117.” She also “sold painting canvasses to Van Gogh,” whom she described as “ugly as sin” with a “vile temper and smelled of booze.”

### Jiroemon Kimura - Oldest man ever

At the time of his death, Jiroemon Kimura had 7 children, 14 grandchildren, 25 great-grandchildren and 14 great-great-grandchildren - Photo credit: Getty

Jiroemon Kimura lived to be 116 years and 54 days old. The Japanese supercentenarian was born on 19 April 1897 and lived through to 12 June 2013. The Guinness World Records quotes him as saying“eat light to live long” and states that he continued to engage in agriculture until he was 90.

### Lucile Randon - 118

Another Frenchwoman, Lucile Randon (see main picture) lived to the age of 118 years and 340 days old. Born on 11 February 1904, she passed away on 17 January 2023.

### Kane Tanaka - 119

Born on 2 January 1903 and passing away on 19 April 2022, the Japanese woman lived to be 119 years and 107 days old.

### Chiyo Miyako - 117

Another Japanese woman, Chiyo Miyako was born on 2 May 1901 and died on 22 July 2018, living up to the ripe age of 117 years and 81 days old.

### Nabi Tajima - 117

117-year-old Nabi Tajima © JIJI PRESS/AFP via Getty Images

Yet another Japanese supercentenarian, Nabi Tajima lived to be 117 years and 260 days old, from her birth on 4 August 1900 to her death on 21 April 2018.

### Violet Brown - 117

We head to Jamaica next and to Violet Brown. She lived to be 117 years and 189 days old. She was born on 10 March 1900 and passed away on 15 September 2017.

### Emma Martina Luigia Morano - 117

Emma Morano in 2016 © OLIVIER MORIN/AFP via Getty Images

Next is Emma Martina Luigia Morano. The Italian supercentenarian also lived to be 117 years old (plus 137 days) and was born on 29 November 1899 before her death on 15 April 2017.

### María Branyas Morera - 117

When María Branyas Morera died aged 117 in August 2024 aged 117 years 168 days, she was the eighth-oldest person (with a verifiable age) in history.

She was born on 4th March 1907 in San Francisco, California, and lived in Texas and New Orleans before her Spanish family returned to Catalonia during World War I, according to Guinness World Records.

She said she lived “an orderly life that is socially very pleasant… a good life, without excesses.”

### Susannah Mushatt Jones - 116

Next up we have Susannah Mushatt Jones from the USA. She lived to be 116 years and 311 days old and was born on 6 July 1899 and died on 12 May 2016.

### Jeralean Talley - 116

World's former oldest person Jeralean Talley in 2015 - Photo credit: Getty

Finally, we have Jeralean Talley, who was also from the USA. She lived to be 116 years and 25 days old. She was born on 23 May 1899 and passed away on 17 June 2015.

Costa Rica’s Civil Registry says that on July 11, 1907—119 years ago—a woman named Josefa in the province of Guanacaste, on the country’s north Pacific coast, gave birth to a boy who was christened José Flores Flores. Everyone born in that first decade of the 20th century, and many who were born years later, are now deceased. But Mr. José still lives in good health in a rural municipality on the edge of a “blue zone,” a name given to regions with unusually high numbers [of centenarians](https://english.elpais.com/lifestyle/2025-08-10/hard-lives-with-days-of-wine-and-roses-the-secrets-of-centenarians-in-spain.html) thanks to healthy living conditions.

What the official registry of the Central American country does not report is that Mr. José is strong, that he has a smile on his face and muscles on his arms, that he sleeps well and eats as well as can be expected in a poor, rural household where he is cared for by family. He is, without a doubt, the oldest person in Costa Rica and possibly in the entire world — a potential record that still depends on certifications being processed by relatives with the help of a local organization and a Spanish researcher who does not hesitate to call Flores “an absolutely extraordinary case.”

We found him in his wooden-and-sheet-metal house located on someone else’s estate in the small village of Obandito de Sardinal, in the hot municipality of Carrillo, near the Nicoya Peninsula. It is part of Guanacaste province, where he returned in 2024 nearly a century after leaving to work on banana plantations in the south of the country, when the region was far from being the destination for the thousands of foreign tourists who now arrive each year drawn by its beaches — and by the rural environment that partly explains the abundance of local [long-lived people](https://english.elpais.com/health/2026-03-21/100-experts-were-unable-to-agree-on-whether-aging-is-an-illness-or-when-it-begins.html).

“Con toda la pata (doing great),” Flores replies to the greeting as he rests seated next to some balloons left over from a recent birthday party, after a breakfast of gallo pinto (rice and beans), fresh cheese and slices of fried plantain. Beside the table where he sometimes plays dominoes or cards, he greets visitors with a strong handshake and a slow but genuine smile. He is now famous in the village and beyond; his dark face appears in local media wearing the Batman cap that belonged to a son who has since died. He has trouble hearing and suffers from knee wear; he says he feels “worn and blunt,” comparing himself to a dull machete. He uses a walker to go outside and feel the breeze, listen to the parrots in the trees and greet neighbors, accompanied by his granddaughter Hellen Flores, who divides her time between caring for her grandfather and attending courses for eldercare because she has discovered a calling and a possible employment opportunity.

José Flores Flores in Sardinal de Carrillo on July 11.Álvaro Murillo

“Many people see grandparents as furniture; they feed them and clean them, but they are not always seen as people with full rights. Here, [José] has the final say over his belongings,” says the granddaughter, who decided to take charge of his care despite not having a fixed income. The family receives only about 150,000 colones a month (about $330), one‑eighth of the average household income in the country. Poverty has accompanied José since he was born in another Guanacaste municipality, where his grandmother raised him after he was abandoned by his mother and lost his father at age seven.

As a child he learned to work in the fields and, barely a teenager, migrated to earn his own money in the banana enclaves in the south of the country, in exchange for brutal workdays in conditions that no one would associate with a long, pleasant or healthy life, except for the advantages of daily physical exercise. Later, married with children, he moved to the country’s north, without ever having the wages to buy his own land. At one point the State was going to allocate him a plot, but he was almost 75 and did not qualify because no one believed he would be able to work it, his granddaughter recalls with a laugh. Now they live in precarious conditions despite various promises of decent housing never being fulfilled, but José always knew how to endure hardship.

“Work a lot, entrust yourself to God and eat healthy.” That is the key José gives. His wife, Ofelia, died at 71. “I can say he reflects that functional lifestyle of the region: family and community networks, organic food, constant physical activity and the calm of a simple life, a routine marked by sunlight, a spirituality tied to religion… it’s a mix of many things,” says Jorge Vindas, founder of the Península de Nicoya Blue Zone Association. This group promotes and protects this part of Guanacaste as a region with a high presence of centenarians, as recorded 20 years ago by U.S. researcher Dan Buettner when he launched an international project that also includes Loma Linda in California, Sardinia in Italy, Ikaria in Greece and the Japanese island of Okinawa. Singapore has recently been added, as a result of large government investments that neither Mr. José nor his granddaughter can possibly imagine.

Flores, however, is not a “product” of Guanacaste’s blue zone. Vindas jokes that “he just left for a century and came back.” The truth is he largely shared the province’s lifestyle, which is now undergoing deep changes accelerated by the tourism industry and an influx of new residents who are altering the environment and influencing locals’ habits. Almost two million travelers arrived directly at Guanacaste Airport in 2025; English-language signs line the roads offering services and properties. Tourism and property developments are displacing vast estates and agricultural plots. Very little remains of the subsistence economy that allowed certain generations to eat without consuming [any processed foods](https://english.elpais.com/society/2023-05-24/ultra-processed-products-lets-not-call-them-food-because-they-arent.html), another health factor that specialists often emphasize.

José Flores Flores and his granddaughter Hellen Flores.Álvaro Murillo

“There are many ingredients in this salad called [longevity](https://english.elpais.com/science-tech/2026-05-25/longevity-researcher-juan-carlos-izpisua-presents-latest-data-on-aging-process-it-is-a-loss-of-identity-at-the-cellular-level.html). Genetics, diet, physical activity… now we have added human relationships and social connection. But there is no definitive answer that explains everything, because other people in similar conditions have died at much younger ages,” says José Antonio Rabadán, PhD in Gerontology from the University of Alicante in Spain and a researcher of the Guanacaste region in Costa Rica, where he has made more than 70 visits to centenarians.

Rabadán met Flores when the latter turned 117 and was impressed by his physical condition. “At 119 years there is no normal. These are cases we are only beginning to understand,” the researcher says of the man who at 113 still walked a kilometer every day to meet other older adults at a daytime center in the town where he then lived. Rabadán is optimistic about obtaining international certification for José. This is because the state registry is reliable, and he also has a copy of the baptismal record signed by Bishop Luis Leipod in 1907.

“There is a very complete file that, to us, gives every credibility to José’s life, with official and verified documents,” adds Rabadán, who is confident of a favorable response from the validating body, the Gerontology Research Group (GRG), a global organization founded in the United States that registers and studies supercentenarians, people older than 110. After that he might become a Guinness World Record holder, but he warns he prefers to take it step by step. So far the oldest living person is the Englishwoman Ethel Caterham, who will turn 117 on August 21, according to GRC data. As far as is known, the record is held by the Frenchwoman Jeanne Calment, who reached 122 years and 164 days and died in 1997.

Rabadán and Vindas know Flores is exceptional as an individual, but he is also part of specific Guanacaste generations with longevity advantages that are disappearing in newer cohorts, as noted since 2023 by the respected demographer Luis Rosero‑Bixby, founder of the Central American Population Center (CCP) at the public University of Costa Rica (UCR). The specialist warned, however, that those born before the 1930s still show exceptionally high longevity in this region of the country, which in any case has a higher life expectancy at birth than the international average (83.7 years for women and 78.6 years for men, according to official figures).

These high ages combine, however, with a national trend of declining fertility to just 1.1 children per woman, which accelerates population aging and strains the economy, the [state welfare model](https://english.elpais.com/international/2026-06-28/the-engine-of-costa-ricas-welfare-system-is-in-intensive-care.html) and pension systems. The granddaughter Hellen, for example, has only one child, who helps her care for his great‑grandfather. “A nursing home? Over my dead body. Here we care for him between my mother, my son and me; this is his home and this is his family,” the woman adds as José smiles without taking his eyes off the television set, where he enjoys watching the 1960s U.S. series Bonanza. He says he enjoys arm sports and squares up to try a strength test with his left arm, his stronger one.

Oldest living people | Gerontology Wiki | Fandom

This is a list of the oldest living people in the world. Supercentenarians that are categorized as "validated" have had their ages authenticated by an organization that specializes in age validation, such as the Gerontology Research Group(GRG), LongeviQuest(LQ), the Guinness World Records(GWR) or International Database on Longevity(IDL).

Supercentenarians that are categorized as "pending validation" have their ages partially authenticated, but remain to be fully processed by an age validation organization. The last group, "unvalidated", refers to supercentenarians that have not had their ages authenticated but for whom there is sufficient reliable-source reporting to at least have a claimed date of birth. However, only claimants age 110–114 that could potentially be validated in the future are included here, although exaggerated claims 115-129 can be found at Living longevity claims, and those false claims above 130 can be found at Living longevity myths.

Since the death of 116-year-old Inah Canabarro Lucas of Brazil on 30 April 2025, 116-year-old Ethel Caterham of the UK is the oldest living person whose age is validated. There are currently 266 validated living supercentenarians by either the Gerontology Research Group(GRG) on the GRG World Supercentenarian Rankings List(WSRL), or by LongeviQuest(LQ) on their list of oldest living people, whom 235 are female and 31 are male.

Synopsis

José Flores Flores, a Costa Rican farmer, celebrated his 119th birthday on July 11. His family is seeking international validation for his exceptional longevity claim. He lives in a recognized Blue Zone known for its healthy inhabitants. Flores remains active and enjoys simple daily activities and games. He previously survived COVID-19 and voted in the 2026 presidential election.

![José Flores Flores, world's oldest person alive](https://img.etimg.com/thumb/msid-132758187,width-650,height-488,imgsize-2317549,resizemode-75/jos-flores-flores-worlds-oldest-person-alive.jpg)

José Flores Flores (Image courtesy: X/@ldacr)

A [Costa Rican farmer](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/topic/costa-rican-farmer) whose reported age is supported by civil and church records has celebrated his 119th birthday, with his family now working to secure international recognition that could make him the [world's oldest living person](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/topic/worlds-oldest-living-person). [José Flores Flores](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/topic/jos%C3%A9-flores-flores), who was born on July 11, 1907, in Las Lajas de Cañas, Guanacaste, marked his birthday on Saturday. While he is officially recognized as Costa Rica's oldest living citizen, his age has yet to be independently verified by [Guinness World Records](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/topic/guinness-world-records) or an international organization specializing in validating claims of exceptional longevity.

As per multiple outlets, including Ticotimes, Costa Rican civil records list Flores' birth date as July 11, 1907, while a baptismal record reportedly shows he was baptized five months later. However, record-verification organizations require sufficient documentation linking records from different stages of a person's life before recognizing longevity claims.

If his age is officially validated, Flores would surpass the current Guinness World Records titleholder by more than two years.

## Could José Flores Flores become the world's oldest living person?

![ET logo](https://img.etimg.com/photo/118783427.cms)

### Live Events

Guinness World Records currently recognizes British woman [Ethel Caterham](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/topic/ethel-caterham) as the world's oldest living person. Caterham was born on August 21, 1909, and was 116 years and 223 days old when her record was verified on April 1, 2026. She is now 116 years and nearly 11 months old.

As per the outlet, Flores' family is gathering historical documents needed to submit his case for international review. If accepted, his reported age of 119 would make him the oldest verified living person in the world.

## Life in one of the world's Blue Zones

Flores lives near Costa Rica's Nicoya Peninsula in Guanacaste, one of the world's five recognized "Blue Zones," regions known for having unusually high numbers of people who live beyond 90 or even 100 years. According to Healthline, other than this, there are 4 more [blue zones](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/topic/blue-zones) in the world located in Okinawa, Japan; Sardinia, Italy; Ikaria, Greece; and Loma Linda, California. These regions are known for having unusually high numbers of people who live to 100 or beyond, a longevity often linked to healthy diets, regular physical activity, strong social connections, and a clear sense of purpose in life.Scientists often attribute the region's longevity to several interconnected lifestyle factors, including diets rich in beans, corn, squash and fresh produce, lifelong physical activity through farming and manual labor, strong family relationships, close-knit communities, a clear sense of purpose later in life, known as "plan de vida."

## A simple lifestyle at 119

As per ticotimes, Flores continues to walk, speak, and eat without assistance. He spends time with family members and neighbors, enjoys watching boxing and movies, and regularly plays dominoes, a game his relatives say he often wins. He reportedly takes just one daily medication to control his blood pressure.His eating habits have remained remarkably consistent over the years. Rice and beans have long been staples of his diet, alongside cheese, tortillas, milk, and vegetables. He eats little meat and has previously said he smoked and drank alcohol when he was younger before eventually giving up both habits. According to the outlet, he usually goes to bed around 7 p.m.

## A lifetime shaped by farming and history

Flores spent much of his life working in agriculture. As a young man, he traveled across different parts of Costa Rica seeking farm and plantation work before settling in Santa Rosa de Pocosol, San Carlos, in 1968. He remained there for more than 50 years before moving to the Sardinal area of Carrillo, where he now lives with family members.He married Ofelia Arias Badilla, who died at the age of 71. Together they had 16 children, eight of whom are still alive. Family accounts also identify Flores as having participated in Costa Rica's 1948 civil war.

## Surviving COVID-19 and making history at the ballot box

Flores has also found himself at the center of several remarkable moments in recent Costa Rican history. In 2021, he became the country's oldest known person to recover from COVID-19. According to his relatives, he experienced no serious symptoms and was initially not told about his diagnosis because family members feared it would worry him. He later recovered from another infection in 2022.During severe flooding in Guanacaste in 2023, Flores was evacuated by helicopter after rising waters threatened his safety. Relatives said he remained calm despite having little previous experience flying.He also became Costa Rica's oldest voter during the country's 2026 presidential election. At 118, Flores cast his ballot in the February 1 vote from Sardinal. Before the election, his family said it would be the 25th time he had voted during his lifetime.
